shloka_text: अर्जुनेन विमुक्तस्तु रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । चचार पृथिवीं सर्वामनिर्विण्णस्तथा कृतः ।। 7.34.1 ।।
transliteration: arjunena vimuktastu rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ | cacāra pṛthivīṃ sarvāmanirviṇṇastathā kṛtaḥ || 7.34.1 ||
translation: अर्जुनेन by Arjuna, विमुक्तः released, तु indeed, रावणः Ravana, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of Rakshasas, चचार roamed, पृथिवीम् earth, सर्वाम् all, अनिर्विण्णः undeterred, तथा thus, कृतः having been treated.
explanation: Indeed, Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, having been released by Arjuna and treated in such a manner, roamed all over the earth undeterred.
comments: Ravana challenges Vali at Kishkindha; warned that Vali is away at the four oceans and invincible, he goes to seize him from behind -- but Vali, unconcerned, tucks Ravana under his arm and carries him round all four oceans as he performs his twilight prayers -- awed, Ravana sues for friendship, sealed by fire, and after a month is led home -- yet even such a Vali, Agastya notes, was slain by Rama.

shloka_text: राक्षसं वा मनुष्यं वा शृणुते ऽयं बलाधिकम् । रावणस्तं समासाद्य युद्धे ह्वयति दर्पितः ।। 7.34.2 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasaṃ vā manuṣyaṃ vā śṛṇute 'yaṃ balādhikam | rāvaṇastaṃ samāsādya yuddhe hvayati darpitaḥ || 7.34.2 ||
translation: राक्षसम् a Rakshasa, वा or, मनुष्यम् a human, वा or, शृणुते hears, अयम् this (Ravana), बलाधिकम् superior in strength, रावणः Ravana, तम् him, समासाद्य having approached, युद्धे in battle, ह्वयति challenges, दर्पितः arrogant.
explanation: This arrogant Ravana, upon hearing of any Rakshasa or human superior in strength, would approach them and challenge them to battle.

shloka_text: ततः कदाचित्किष्किन्धां नगरीं वालिपालिताम् । गत्वा ह्वयति युद्धाय वालिनं हेममालिनम् ।। 7.34.3 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ kadācitkiṣkindhāṃ nagarīṃ vālipālitām | gatvā hvayati yuddhāya vālinaṃ hemamālinam || 7.34.3 ||
translation: ततः Then, कदाचित् once, किष्किन्धां to Kishkindha, नगरीं city, वालिपालिताम् protected by Vali, गत्वा having gone, ह्वयति challenges, युद्धाय for battle, वालिनं Vali, हेममालिनम् adorned with a golden garland.
explanation: Then, once, having gone to the city of Kishkindha, which was protected by Vali, he challenged Vali, who was adorned with a golden garland, for battle.

shloka_text: ततस्तु वानरामात्यस्तारस्तारापिता प्रभुः । उवाच वानरो वाक्यं युद्धप्रेप्सुमुपागतम् ।। 7.34.4 ।।
transliteration: tatastu vānarāmātyastārastārāpitā prabhuḥ | uvāca vānaro vākyaṃ yuddhaprepsumupāgatam || 7.34.4 ||
translation: ततस्तु But then, वानरामात्यः the minister of monkeys, तारस्तारापिता Sushena (father of Tara), प्रभुः the powerful one, उवाच spoke, वानरः the monkey, वाक्यं words, युद्धप्रेप्सुम् to the one desirous of battle, उपागतम् who had come near.
explanation: But then, Sushena, the powerful minister of the monkeys and father of Tara, spoke words to the one who had come near, desirous of battle.

shloka_text: राक्षसेन्द गतो वाली यस्ते प्रतिबलो भवेत् । को ऽन्यः प्रमुखतः स्थातुं तव शक्तः प्लवङ्गमः ।। 7.34.5 ।।
transliteration: rākṣasenda gato vālī yaste pratibalo bhavet | ko 'nyaḥ pramukhataḥ sthātuṃ tava śaktaḥ plavaṅgamaḥ || 7.34.5 ||
translation: राक्षसेन्द O king of Rakshasas, गतो gone, वाली Vali, यः who, ते to you, प्रतिबलो an equal opponent, भवेत् would be; को ऽन्यः who else, प्रमुखतः in front of, स्थातुं to stand, तव your, शक्तः capable, प्लवङ्गमः monkey (is there)?
explanation: O king of Rakshasas, Vali, who would be an equal opponent to you, has departed; what other monkey is capable of standing before you?

shloka_text: चतुर्भ्यो ऽपि समुद्रेभ्यः सन्ध्यामन्वास्य रावण । इमं मुहूर्तमायाति वाली तिष्ठ मुहूर्तकम् ।। 7.34.6 ।।
transliteration: caturbhyo 'pi samudrebhyaḥ sandhyāmanvāsya rāvaṇa | imaṃ muhūrtamāyāti vālī tiṣṭha muhūrtakam || 7.34.6 ||
translation: चतुर्भ्यो ऽपि from all four, समुद्रेभ्यः oceans, सन्ध्याम् twilight prayers, अन्वास्य having performed, रावण O Ravana, इमं this, मुहूर्तम् moment, आयाति is coming, वाली Vali; तिष्ठ wait, मुहूर्तकम् for a moment.
explanation: O Ravana, Vali is returning in a moment, having performed his twilight prayers from all four oceans; wait for just a moment.

shloka_text: एतानस्थिचयान्पश्य य एते शङ्खपाण्डुराः । युद्धार्थिनामिमे राजन्वानराधिपतेजसा ।। 7.34.7 ।।
transliteration: etānasthicayānpaśya ya ete śaṅkhapāṇḍurāḥ | yuddhārthināmime rājanvānarādhipatejasā || 7.34.7 ||
translation: एतान् these, अस्थिचयान् piles of bones, पश्य behold, यः which, एते these, शङ्खपाण्डुराः conch-white, युद्धार्थिनाम् of those desirous of battle, इमे these, राजन् O king, वानराधिपतेजसा by the might of the king of monkeys.
explanation: O king, behold these conch-white piles of bones, which are the remains of those who desired battle, vanquished by the might of the king of monkeys.

shloka_text: यद्वा ऽमृतरसः पीतस्त्वया रावण राक्षस । तदा वालिनमासाद्य तदन्तं तव जीवितम् ।। 7.34.8 ।।
transliteration: yadvā 'mṛtarasaḥ pītastvayā rāvaṇa rākṣasa | tadā vālinamāsādya tadantaṃ tava jīvitam || 7.34.8 ||
translation: यद्वा or if, अमृतरसः the nectar of immortality, पीतः has been drunk, त्वया by you, रावण O Ravana, राक्षस O demon, तदा then, वालिनम् Valin, आसाद्य having met, तदन्तम् its end, तव your, जीवितम् life.
explanation: O demon Ravana, even if you have drunk the nectar of immortality, your life will surely end once you encounter Valin.

shloka_text: पश्येदानीं जगच्चित्रमिमं विश्रवसः सुत । इदं मुहूर्तं तिष्ठस्व दुर्लभं ते भविष्यति ।। 7.34.9 ।।
transliteration: paśyedānīṃ jagaccitramimaṃ viśravasaḥ suta | idaṃ muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭhasva durlabhaṃ te bhaviṣyati || 7.34.9 ||
translation: पश्य behold, इदानीम् now, जगच्चित्रम् the wonder of the world, इमम् this, विश्रवसः of Vishravas, सुत O son, इदम् this, मुहूर्तम् moment, तिष्ठस्व stay, दुर्लभम् rare, ते for you, भविष्यति it will be.
explanation: O son of Vishravas, behold this wonder of the world now, and wait for a moment, for such an opportunity will be rare for you in the future.

shloka_text: अथवा त्वरसे मर्तुं गच्छ दक्षिणसागरम् । वालिनं द्रक्ष्यसे तत्र भूमिस्थमिव पावकम् ।। 7.34.10 ।।
transliteration: athavā tvarase martuṃ gaccha dakṣiṇasāgaram | vālinaṃ drakṣyase tatra bhūmisthamiva pāvakam || 7.34.10 ||
translation: अथवा or, त्वरसे you hasten, मर्तुम् to die, गच्छ go, दक्षिणसागरम् to the southern ocean, वालिनम् Valin, द्रक्ष्यसे you will see, तत्र there, भूमिस्थम् standing on the ground, इव like, पावकम् fire.
explanation: Alternatively, if you are eager to die, go to the southern ocean, where you will see Valin, who is like a fire standing on the earth.

shloka_text: स तु तारं विनिर्भर्त्स्य रावणो लोकरावणः । पुष्पकं तत्समारुह्य प्रययौ दक्षिणार्णवम् ।। 7.34.11 ।।
transliteration: sa tu tāraṃ vinirbhartsya rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ | puṣpakaṃ tatsamāruhya prayayau dakṣiṇārṇavam || 7.34.11 ||
translation: सः he, तु indeed, तारम् Tara, विनिर्भर्त्स्य having severely rebuked, रावणः Ravana, लोकरावणः the tormentor of the worlds, पुष्पकम् Pushpaka, तत् that, समारुह्य having ascended, प्रययौ he set off, दक्षिणार्णवम् to the southern ocean.
explanation: Indeed, that Ravana, the tormentor of the worlds, having severely rebuked Tara, ascended his Pushpaka chariot and set off towards the southern ocean.

shloka_text: तत्र हेमगिरिप्रख्यं तरुणार्कनिभाननम् । रावणो वालिनं दृष्ट्वा सन्ध्योपासनतत्परम् ।। 7.34.12 ।।
transliteration: tatra hemagiriprakhyaṃ taruṇārkanibhānanam | rāvaṇo vālinaṃ dṛṣṭvā sandhyopāsanatatparam || 7.34.12 ||
translation: तत्र there, हेमगिरिप्रख्यम् resembling a golden mountain, तरुणार्कनिभाननम् whose face resembled the rising sun, रावणः Ravana, वालिनम् Valin, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सन्ध्योपासनतत्परम् intent on performing his twilight prayers.
explanation: There, Ravana saw Valin, who resembled a golden mountain with a face like the rising sun, intently engaged in his twilight prayers.

shloka_text: पुष्पकादवरुह्याथ रावणो ऽञ्जनसन्निभः । ग्रहीतुं वालिनं तूर्णं निःशब्दपदमाव्रजत् ।। 7.34.13 ।।
transliteration: puṣpakādavaruhyātha rāvaṇo 'ñjanasannibhaḥ | grahītuṃ vālinaṃ tūrṇaṃ niḥśabdapadamāvrajat || 7.34.13 ||
translation: पुष्पकात् from Pushpaka, अवरुह्य having descended, अथ then, रावणः Ravana, अञ्जनसन्निभः resembling collyrium, ग्रहीतुम् to seize, वालिनम् Valin, तूर्णं quickly, निःशब्दपदम् with silent steps, आव्रजत् approached.
explanation: Then, Ravana, dark like collyrium, descended from the Pushpaka chariot and quickly approached Valin with silent steps, intending to seize him.

shloka_text: यदृच्छया तदा दृष्टो वालिनापि स रावणः । पापाभिप्रायवान् दृष्ट्वा चकार न तु सम्भ्रमम् ।। 7.34.14 ।।
transliteration: yadṛcchayā tadā dṛṣṭo vālināpi sa rāvaṇaḥ | pāpābhiprāyavān dṛṣṭvā cakāra na tu sambhramam || 7.34.14 ||
translation: यदृच्छया by chance, तदा then, दृष्टः seen, वालिना by Valin, अपि also, सः that, रावणः Ravana, पापाभिप्रायवान् having evil intentions, दृष्ट्वा having seen, चकार made, न not, तु but, सम्भ्रमम् agitation.
explanation: By chance, Valin then saw that Ravana, who had evil intentions, but upon seeing him, Valin showed no agitation.

shloka_text: शशमालक्ष्य सिंहो वा पन्नगं गरुडो यथा । न चिन्तयति तं वाली रावणं पापनिश्चयम् ।। 7.34.15 ।।
transliteration: śaśamālakṣya siṃho vā pannagaṃ garuḍo yathā | na cintayati taṃ vālī rāvaṇaṃ pāpaniścayam || 7.34.15 ||
translation: शशम् a rabbit, आलक्ष्य having seen, सिंहः a lion, वा or, पन्नगम् a serpent, गरुडः Garuda, यथा just as, न not, चिन्तयति considers, तम् him, वाली Valin, रावणम् Ravana, पापनिश्चयम् evil-minded.
explanation: Just as a lion does not worry about a rabbit, or Garuda about a serpent, so Valin did not consider that evil-minded Ravana a threat.

shloka_text: जिघृक्षमाणमायान्तं रावणं पापचेतसम् । कक्षावलम्बिनं कृत्वा गमिष्ये त्रीन्महार्णवान् ।। 7.34.16 ।।
transliteration: jighṛkṣamāṇamāyāntaṃ rāvaṇaṃ pāpacetasam | kakṣāvalambinaṃ kṛtvā gamiṣye trīnmahārṇavān || 7.34.16 ||
translation: जिघृक्षमाणम् wishing to seize, आयान्तम् coming, रावणम् Ravana, पापचेतसम् evil-minded, कक्षावलम्बिनम् hanging from the armpit, कृत्वा having made, गमिष्ये I shall go, त्रीन् three, महार्णवान् great oceans.
explanation: Valin thought, "I will make this evil-minded Ravana, who is coming to seize me, hang from my armpit and then I shall traverse the three great oceans."

shloka_text: द्रक्ष्यन्त्यरिं ममाङ्कस्थं स्रंसदूरुकराम्बरम् । लम्बमानं दशग्रीवं गरुडस्येव पन्नगम् ।। 7.34.17 ।।
transliteration: drakṣyantyariṃ mamāṅkasthaṃ sraṃsadūrukarāmbaram | lambamānaṃ daśagrīvaṃ garuḍasyeva pannagam || 7.34.17 ||
translation: द्रक्ष्यन्ति they will see, अरिम् the enemy, मम my, अङ्कस्थम् on the side, स्रंसत् slipping, ऊरु thighs, कर hands, अम्बरम् clothes, लम्बमानम् hanging, दशग्रीवम् Dashagriva, गरुडस्य of Garuda, इव like, पन्नगम् a serpent.
explanation: Valin further thought, "They will see my enemy Dashagriva, with his thighs, hands, and clothes slipping, hanging from my side like a serpent from Garuda."

shloka_text: इत्येवं मतिमास्थाय वाली कर्णमुपाश्रितः । जपन्वै नैगमान्मन्त्रांस्तस्थौ पर्वतराडिव ।। 7.34.18 ।।
transliteration: ityevaṃ matimāsthāya vālī karṇamupāśritaḥ | japanvai naigamānmantrāṃstasthau parvatarāḍiva || 7.34.18 ||
translation: इत्येवं thus, मतिम् resolve, आस्थाय having adopted, वाली Vali, कर्णम् a secluded spot, उपाश्रितः having resorted to, जपन् chanting, वै indeed, नैगमान् Vedic, मन्त्रान् mantras, तस्थौ stood, पर्वतराट् king of mountains, इव like.
explanation: Vali, having adopted this resolve, resorted to a secluded spot and stood there, chanting Vedic mantras, appearing like the king of mountains.

shloka_text: तावन्योन्यं जिघृक्षन्तौ हरिराक्षसपार्थिवौ । प्रयत्नवन्तौ तत्कर्म ईहतुर्बलदर्पितौ ।। 7.34.19 ।।
transliteration: tāvanyonyaṃ jighṛkṣantau harirākṣasapārthivau | prayatnavantau tatkarma īhaturbaladarpitau || 7.34.19 ||
translation: तौ those two, अन्योन्यम् each other, जिघृक्षन्तौ desiring to seize, हरि monkey (Vali), राक्षस demon (Ravana), पार्थिवौ kings, प्रयत्नवन्तौ making effort, तत्कर्म that action, ईहतुः they performed, बलदर्पितौ proud of their strength.
explanation: Those two kings, Vali and Ravana, both proud of their strength and desiring to seize each other, engaged in that struggle with great effort.

shloka_text: हस्तग्राहं तु तं मत्वा पादशब्देन रावणम् । पराङ्मुखो ऽपि जग्राह वाली सर्पमिवाण्डजः ।। 7.34.20 ।।
transliteration: hastagrāhaṃ tu taṃ matvā pādaśabdena rāvaṇam | parāṅmukho 'pi jagrāha vālī sarpamivāṇḍajaḥ || 7.34.20 ||
translation: हस्तग्राहम् within reach of hand, तु indeed, तम् him, मत्वा having perceived, पादशब्देन by the sound of footsteps, रावणम् Ravana, पराङ्मुखः facing away, अपि even, जग्राह seized, वाली Vali, सर्पम् a snake, इव like, अण्डजः a bird.
explanation: Vali, perceiving Ravana by the sound of his footsteps and considering him within reach, seized him even while facing away, just as a bird seizes a snake.

shloka_text: ग्रहीतुकामं तं गृह्य रक्षसामीश्वरं हरिः । खमुत्पपात वेगेन कृत्वा कक्षावलम्बिनम् ।। 7.34.21 ।।
transliteration: grahītukāmaṃ taṃ gṛhya rakṣasāmīśvaraṃ hariḥ | khamutpapāta vegena kṛtvā kakṣāvalambinam || 7.34.21 ||
translation: ग्रहीतुकामम् desiring to seize (Vali), तम् him, गृह्य having seized, रक्षसाम् of the demons, ईश्वरम् lord, हरिः the monkey (Vali), खम् sky, उत्पपात flew up, वेगेन with speed, कृत्वा having made, कक्षावलम्बिनम् hanging from his armpit.
explanation: The monkey king Vali, having seized Ravana, the lord of demons, who had intended to capture him, swiftly flew up into the sky, holding Ravana hanging from his armpit.

shloka_text: तं चापीडयमानं तु वितुदन्तं नखैर्मुहुः । जहार रावणं वाली पवनस्तोयदं यथा ।। 7.34.22 ।।
transliteration: taṃ cāpīḍayamānaṃ tu vitudantaṃ nakhairmuhuḥ | jahāra rāvaṇaṃ vālī pavanastoyadaṃ yathā || 7.34.22 ||
translation: तम् him, च and, आपीडयमानम् being oppressed, तु indeed, वितुदन्तम् scratching, नखैः with nails, मुहुः repeatedly, जहार carried away, रावणम् Ravana, वाली Vali, पवनः wind, तोयदम् a cloud, यथा just as.
explanation: Vali carried away Ravana, who was being oppressed and repeatedly scratching him with his nails, just as the wind carries away a cloud.

shloka_text: अथ ते राक्षसामात्या ह्रियमाणं दशाननम् । मुमोक्षयिषवो वालिं रवमाणा अभिद्रुताः ।। 7.34.23 ।।
transliteration: atha te rākṣasāmātyā hriyamāṇaṃ daśānanam | mumokṣayiṣavo vāliṃ ravamāṇā abhidrutāḥ || 7.34.23 ||
translation: अथ then, ते those, राक्षसामात्याः Rakshasa ministers, ह्रियमाणं being carried away, दशाननम् Dashanana (Ravana), मुमोक्षयिषवः desiring to free, वालिं from Vali, रवमाणाः shouting, अभिद्रुताः rushed after.
explanation: Then, those Rakshasa ministers, seeing Dashanana being carried away by Vali, rushed after him, shouting, desiring to free their king.

shloka_text: अन्वीयमानस्तैर्वाली भ्राजते ऽम्बरमध्यगः । अन्वीयमानो मेघौघैरम्बरस्थ इवांशुमान् ।। 7.34.24 ।।
transliteration: anvīyamānastairvālī bhrājate 'mbaramadhyagaḥ | anvīyamāno meghaughairambarastha ivāṃśumān || 7.34.24 ||
translation: अन्वीयमानः being followed, तैः by them, वाली Vali, भ्राजते shone, अम्बरमध्यगः in the middle of the sky, अन्वीयमानः being followed, मेघौघैः by masses of clouds, अम्बरस्थः situated in the sky, इव like, अंशुमान् the sun.
explanation: Vali, being followed by those Rakshasas in the middle of the sky, shone like the sun in the sky being followed by masses of clouds.

shloka_text: ते ऽशक्नुवन्तः सम्प्राप्तुं वालिनं राक्षसोत्तमाः । तस्य बाहूरुवेगेन परिश्रान्ता व्यवस्थिताः ।। 7.34.25 ।।
transliteration: te 'śaknuvantaḥ samprāptuṃ vālinaṃ rākṣasottamāḥ | tasya bāhūruvegena pariśrāntā vyavasthitāḥ || 7.34.25 ||
translation: ते those, अशक्नुवन्तः being unable, सम्प्राप्तुं to reach, वालिनं Vali, राक्षसोत्तमाः the chief Rakshasas, तस्य his, बाहूरुवेगेन by the speed of his arms and thighs, परिश्रान्ताः exhausted, व्यवस्थिताः stopped.
explanation: Those chief Rakshasas, unable to reach Vali due to his immense speed, became exhausted and stopped.

shloka_text: वालिमार्गादपाक्रामन्पर्वतेन्द्रो हि गच्छतः । किं पुनर्जीवितप्रेप्सुर्बिभ्रद्वै मांसशोणितम् ।। 7.34.26 ।।
transliteration: vālimārgādapākrāmanparvatendro hi gacchataḥ | kiṃ punarjīvitaprepsurbibhradvai māṃsaśoṇitam || 7.34.26 ||
translation: वालिमार्गात् from Vali's path, अपाक्रामन् moved away, पर्वतेन्द्रः even the king of mountains, हि indeed, गच्छतः of one going, किं पुनः what then, जीवितप्रेप्सुः one desiring to live, बिभ्रत् carrying, वै indeed, मांसशोणितम् flesh and blood.
explanation: Indeed, even a great mountain would move away from Vali's path as he flew, so how much more would those Rakshasas, who were mere beings of flesh and blood desiring to live, be unable to keep up.

shloka_text: अपक्षिगणसम्पातान्वानरेन्द्रो महाजवः । क्रमशः सागरान्सर्वान्सन्ध्याकालमवन्दत ।। 7.34.27 ।।
transliteration: apakṣigaṇasampātānvānarendro mahājavaḥ | kramaśaḥ sāgarānsarvānsandhyākālamavandata || 7.34.27 ||
translation: अपक्षिगणसम्पातान् where flocks of birds do not reach, वानरेन्द्रः the king of monkeys, महाजवः of great speed, क्रमशः successively, सागरान् the oceans, सर्वान् all, सन्ध्याकालम् the twilight time, अवन्दत worshipped.
explanation: The immensely swift king of monkeys, Vali, flew through regions where even flocks of birds could not reach, successively worshipping all the oceans as the twilight hour arrived.

shloka_text: सभाज्यमानो भूतैस्तु खैचरैः खैचरोत्तमः । पश्चिमं सागरं वाली ह्याजगाम सरावणः ।। 7.34.28 ।।
transliteration: sabhājyamāno bhūtaistu khaicaraiḥ khaicarottamaḥ | paścimaṃ sāgaraṃ vālī hyājagāma sarāvaṇaḥ || 7.34.28 ||
translation: sabhājyamāno being honored, bhūtaiḥ tu by beings indeed, khaicaraiḥ by sky-dwellers, khaicarottamaḥ the best among sky-dwellers, paścimaṃ western, sāgaraṃ ocean, vālī Vali, hi indeed, ājagāma came, sarāvaṇaḥ with Ravana
explanation: Vali, the best among sky-dwellers, being honored by various celestial beings, indeed reached the western ocean with Ravana.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्सन्ध्यामुपासित्वा स्नात्वा जप्त्वा च वानरः । उत्तरं सागरं प्रायाद्वहमानो दशाननम् ।। 7.34.29 ।।
transliteration: tasminsandhyāmupāsitvā snātvā japtvā ca vānaraḥ | uttaraṃ sāgaraṃ prāyādvahamāno daśānanam || 7.34.29 ||
translation: tasmin there, sandhyām evening prayer, upāsitvā having performed, snātvā having bathed, japtvā having chanted, ca and, vānaraḥ the monkey, uttaraṃ northern, sāgaraṃ ocean, prāyāt proceeded, vahamānaḥ carrying, daśānanam Ravana
explanation: Having performed his evening prayers, bathed, and chanted mantras there, Vali, the monkey, proceeded to the northern ocean, still carrying Ravana.

shloka_text: बहुयोजनसाहस्रं वहमानो महाहरिः । वायुवच्च मनोवच्च जगाम सह शत्रुणा ।। 7.34.30 ।।
transliteration: bahuyojanasāhasraṃ vahamāno mahāhariḥ | vāyuvacca manovacca jagāma saha śatruṇā || 7.34.30 ||
translation: bahuyojanasāhasraṃ many thousands of yojanas, vahamānaḥ carrying, mahāhariḥ the great monkey, vāyuvacca like the wind, manovacca and like the mind, jagāma went, saha with, śatruṇā his enemy
explanation: The great monkey, carrying his enemy for many thousands of yojanas, traveled with the speed of wind and thought.

shloka_text: उत्तरे सागरे सन्ध्यामुपासित्वा दशाननम् । वहमानो ऽगमद्वाली पूर्वं वै स महोदधिम् ।। 7.34.31 ।।
transliteration: uttare sāgare sandhyāmupāsitvā daśānanam | vahamāno 'gamadvālī pūrvaṃ vai sa mahodadhim || 7.34.31 ||
translation: uttare in the northern, sāgare ocean, sandhyām evening prayer, upāsitvā having performed, daśānanam Ravana, vahamānaḥ carrying, agamadvālī Vali went, pūrvaṃ eastern, vai indeed, sa he, mahodadhim great ocean
explanation: After performing his evening prayers in the northern ocean, Vali, still carrying Ravana, then proceeded to the eastern great ocean.

shloka_text: तत्रापि सन्ध्यामन्वास्य वासविः सहरीश्वरः । किष्किन्धामभितो गृह्य रावणं पुनरागमत् ।। 7.34.32 ।।
transliteration: tatrāpi sandhyāmanvāsya vāsaviḥ saharīśvaraḥ | kiṣkindhāmabhito gṛhya rāvaṇaṃ punarāgamat || 7.34.32 ||
translation: tatra api there also, sandhyām evening prayer, anvāsya having performed, vāsaviḥ Vali, saharīśvaraḥ the lord of monkeys, kiṣkindhām Kishkindha, abhitaḥ towards, gṛhya having held, rāvaṇaṃ Ravana, punarāgamat returned again
explanation: Having performed his evening prayers there as well, Vali, the lord of monkeys, returned towards Kishkindha, still holding Ravana.

shloka_text: चतुर्ष्वपि समुद्रेषु सन्ध्यामन्वास्य वानरः । रावणोद्वहनश्रान्तः किष्किन्धोपवने ऽपतत् ।। 7.34.33 ।।
transliteration: caturṣvapi samudreṣu sandhyāmanvāsya vānaraḥ | rāvaṇodvahanaśrāntaḥ kiṣkindhopavane 'patat || 7.34.33 ||
translation: चतुर्ष्वपि in all four, समुद्रेषु oceans, सन्ध्याम् twilight prayers, अन्वास्य having performed, वानरः the monkey (Bali), रावणोद्वहनश्रान्तः tired from carrying Ravana, किष्किन्धोपवने in the pleasure grove of Kishkindha, अपतत् fell down.
explanation: After performing his twilight prayers in all four oceans, the monkey (Bali), exhausted from carrying Ravana, landed in the pleasure grove of Kishkindha.

shloka_text: रावणं तु मुमोचाथ स्वकक्षात्कपिसत्तमः । कुतस्त्वमिति चोवाच प्रहसन्रावणं मुहुः ।। 7.34.34 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇaṃ tu mumocātha svakakṣātkapisattamaḥ | kutastvamiti covāca prahasanrāvaṇaṃ muhuḥ || 7.34.34 ||
translation: रावणम् Ravana, तु indeed, मुमोच released, अथ then, स्वकक्षात् from his armpit, कपिसत्तमः the best of monkeys (Bali), कुतः from where, त्वम् you, इति thus, च and, उवाच said, प्रहसन् laughing, रावणम् to Ravana, मुहुः repeatedly.
explanation: Then, the best of monkeys (Bali) released Ravana from his armpit and, laughing repeatedly, asked Ravana, "Where are you from?"

shloka_text: विस्मयं तु महद्गत्वा श्रमलोलनिरीक्षणः । राक्षसेन्द्रो हरीन्द्रं तमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.34.35 ।।
transliteration: vismayaṃ tu mahadgatvā śramalolanirīkṣaṇaḥ | rākṣasendro harīndraṃ tamidaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.34.35 ||
translation: विस्मयम् astonishment, तु indeed, महत् great, गत्वा having experienced, श्रमलोलनिरीक्षणः whose gaze was unsteady due to fatigue, राक्षसेन्द्रः the king of Rakshasas (Ravana), हरीन्द्रम् to the king of monkeys (Bali), तम् that, इदम् this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having experienced great astonishment and with his gaze unsteady from fatigue, the king of Rakshasas (Ravana) spoke these words to that king of monkeys (Bali).

shloka_text: वानरेन्द्र महेन्द्राभ राक्षसेन्द्रो ऽस्मि रावणः । युद्धेप्सुरिह सम्प्राप्तः स चाद्यासादितस्त्वया ।। 7.34.36 ।।
transliteration: vānarendra mahendrābha rākṣasendro 'smi rāvaṇaḥ | yuddhepsuriha samprāptaḥ sa cādyāsāditastvayā || 7.34.36 ||
translation: वानरेन्द्र O king of monkeys, महेन्द्राभ O one resembling Mahendra, राक्षसेन्द्रः the king of Rakshasas, अस्मि I am, रावणः Ravana, युद्धेप्सुः desirous of battle, इह here, सम्प्राप्तः arrived, सः that (desire for battle), च and, अद्य today, आसादितः obtained, त्वया by you.
explanation: Ravana addressed Bali, saying, "O king of monkeys, resembling Mahendra, I am Ravana, the king of Rakshasas, who arrived here desirous of battle, and that desire has been fulfilled by you today."

shloka_text: अहो बलमहो वीर्यमहो गाम्भीर्यमेव च । येनाहं पशुवद्गृह्य भ्रामितश्चतुरो ऽर्णवान् ।। 7.34.37 ।।
transliteration: aho balamaho vīryamaho gāmbhīryameva ca | yenāhaṃ paśuvadgṛhya bhrāmitaścaturo 'rṇavān || 7.34.37 ||
translation: अहो Oh!, बलम् strength, अहो Oh!, वीर्यम् valor, अहो Oh!, गाम्भीर्यम् profundity, एव indeed, च and, येन by whom, अहम् I, पशुवत् like an animal, गृह्य having been seized, भ्रामितः made to wander, चतुरः four, अर्णवान् oceans.
explanation: Ravana exclaimed, "Oh, what strength, what valor, and what profundity, by which I was seized like an animal and carried around all four oceans!"

shloka_text: एवमश्रान्तवद्वीर शीघ्रमेव महार्णवान् । मां चैवोद्वहमानस्तु को ऽन्यो वीरः क्रमिष्यति ।। 7.34.38 ।।
transliteration: evamaśrāntavadvīra śīghrameva mahārṇavān | māṃ caivodvahamānastu ko 'nyo vīraḥ kramiṣyati || 7.34.38 ||
translation: एवम् thus, अश्रान्तवत् tirelessly, वीर O hero, शीघ्रमेव very quickly, महार्णवान् the great oceans, माम् me, च and, एव indeed, उद्वहमानः carrying, तु indeed, कः who, अन्यः other, वीरः hero, क्रमिष्यति will cross.
explanation: O hero, who else but you, carrying me and the great oceans, will swiftly and tirelessly traverse them?

shloka_text: त्रयाणामेव भूतानां गतिरेषा प्लवङ्गम । मनोनिलसुपर्णानां तव चात्र न संशयः ।। 7.34.39 ।।
transliteration: trayāṇāmeva bhūtānāṃ gatireṣā plavaṅgama | manonilasuparṇānāṃ tava cātra na saṃśayaḥ || 7.34.39 ||
translation: त्रयाणाम् of three, एव indeed, भूतानाम् of beings, गतिः speed, एषा this, प्लवङ्गम O monkey, मनः mind, अनिलः wind, सुपर्णानाम् of Suparna (Garuda), तव your, च and, अत्र in this, न not, संशयः doubt.
explanation: O monkey, this speed belongs to only three beings: the mind, the wind, and Suparna (Garuda), and there is no doubt that it also belongs to you.

shloka_text: सो ऽहं दृष्टबलस्तुभ्यमिच्छामि हरिपुङ्गव । त्वया सह चिरं सख्यं सुस्निग्धं पावकाग्रतः ।। 7.34.40 ।।
transliteration: so 'haṃ dṛṣṭabalastubhyamicchāmi haripuṅgava | tvayā saha ciraṃ sakhyaṃ susnigdhaṃ pāvakāgrataḥ || 7.34.40 ||
translation: सः that, अहम् I, दृष्टबलः one whose strength has been seen, तुभ्यम् by you, इच्छामि I desire, हरिपुङ्गव O best of monkeys, त्वया with you, सह together, चिरम् for a long time, सख्यम् friendship, सुस्निग्धम् very affectionate, पावकाग्रतः in front of fire.
explanation: O best of monkeys, having witnessed your strength, I desire to establish a very firm and lasting friendship with you in the presence of fire.

shloka_text: दाराः पुत्राः पुरं राष्ट्रं भोगाच्छादनभोजनम् । सर्वमेवाविभक्तं नौ भविष्यति हरीश्वर ।। 7.34.41 ।।
transliteration: dārāḥ putrāḥ puraṃ rāṣṭraṃ bhogācchādanabhojanam | sarvamevāvibhaktaṃ nau bhaviṣyati harīśvara || 7.34.41 ||
translation: दाराः wives, पुत्राः sons, पुरम् city, राष्ट्रम् kingdom, भोगाः enjoyments, आच्छादनम् clothing, भोजनम् food, सर्वम् all, एव indeed, अविभक्तम् undivided, नौ for us two, भविष्यति will be, हरीश्वर O lord of monkeys.
explanation: O lord of monkeys, our wives, sons, city, kingdom, enjoyments, clothing, and food, all will indeed be undivided between us.

shloka_text: ततः प्रज्वालयित्वाग्निं तावुभौ हरीराक्षसौ । भ्रातृत्वमुपसम्पन्नौ परिष्वज्य परस्परम् ।। 7.34.42 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prajvālayitvāgniṃ tāvubhau harīrākṣasau | bhrātṛtvamupasampannau pariṣvajya parasparam || 7.34.42 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रज्वालयित्वा having kindled, अग्निम् fire, तौ those two, उभौ both, हरी the monkey, राक्षसौ and the Rakshasa, भ्रातृत्वम् brotherhood, उपसम्पन्नौ having attained, परिष्वज्य having embraced, परस्परम् each other.
explanation: Then, having kindled a fire, both the monkey (Hanuman) and the Rakshasa (Vibhishana) established their brotherhood and embraced each other.

shloka_text: अन्योन्यं लम्बितकरौ ततस्तौ हरिराक्षसौ । किष्किन्धां विशतुर्हृष्टौ सिंहौ गिरिगुहामिव ।। 7.34.43 ।।
transliteration: anyonyaṃ lambitakarau tatastau harirākṣasau | kiṣkindhāṃ viśaturhṛṣṭau siṃhau giriguhāmiva || 7.34.43 ||
translation: अन्योन्यं each other, लम्बितकरौ with hands clasped, ततः then, तौ those two, हरिराक्षसौ the monkey and the demon, किष्किन्धां to Kishkindha, विशतुः entered, हृष्टौ delighted, सिंहौ two lions, गिरिगुहाम् a mountain cave, इव like,
explanation: Then, those two, the monkey (Vali) and the demon (Ravana), with hands clasped, joyfully entered Kishkindha, just like two lions entering a mountain cave.

shloka_text: स तत्र मासमुषितः सुग्रीव इव रावणः । अमात्यैरागतैर्नीतस्त्रैलोक्योत्सादनार्थिभिः ।। 7.34.44 ।।
transliteration: sa tatra māsamuṣitaḥ sugrīva iva rāvaṇaḥ | amātyairāgatairnītastrailokyotsādanārthibhiḥ || 7.34.44 ||
translation: सः he, तत्र there, मासम् for a month, उषितः having stayed, सुग्रीवः Sugriva, इव like, रावणः Ravana, अमात्यैः by ministers, आगतैः who had arrived, नीतः was led away, त्रैलोक्य of the three worlds, उत्सादन destruction, अर्थिभिः desiring,
explanation: Ravana, having stayed there for a month like Sugriva, was then led away by his ministers who had arrived, desiring the destruction of the three worlds.

shloka_text: एवमेतत्पुरावृत्तं वालिना रावणः प्रभो । धर्षितश्च कृतश्चापि भ्राता पावकसन्निधौ ।। 7.34.45 ।।
transliteration: evametatpurāvṛttaṃ vālinā rāvaṇaḥ prabho | dharṣitaśca kṛtaścāpi bhrātā pāvakasannidhau || 7.34.45 ||
translation: एवम् thus, एतत् this, पुरा formerly, वृत्तम् happened, वालिना by Vali, रावणः Ravana, प्रभो O Lord, धर्षितः humiliated, च and, कृतः made, च and, अपि also, भ्राता a brother, पावक fire, सन्निधौ in the presence of,
explanation: O Lord, thus did this happen formerly: Ravana was humiliated by Vali and also made his brother in the presence of fire.

shloka_text: बलमप्रतिमं राम वालिनो ऽभवदुत्तमम् । सो ऽपि त्वया विनिर्दग्धः शलभो वह्निना यथा ।। 7.34.46 ।।
transliteration: balamapratimaṃ rāma vālino 'bhavaduttamam | so 'pi tvayā vinirdagdhaḥ śalabho vahninā yathā || 7.34.46 ||
translation: बलम् strength, अप्रतिमम् unequalled, राम O Rama, वालिनः of Vali, अभवत् was, उत्तमम् supreme, सः he, अपि even, त्वया by you, विनिर्दग्धः completely destroyed, शलभः a moth, वह्निना by fire, यथा just as,
explanation: O Rama, Vali possessed supreme and unequalled strength, yet even he was completely destroyed by you, just as a moth is consumed by fire. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुस्त्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 34 ।। Thus ends the thirty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
